Description
The SCRATCH HARDNESS TESTER 430 P-Smart is an electromotive, all-purpose tester designed for scratching and cutting tasks on paint coats and plastic surfaces. It enables individual cuts, parallel cuts, and cross-hatch cuts (after rotating the sample 90) on test plates of varying thicknesses. This tester is particularly suited for adhesion tests using the cross-hatch method according to all common standards, as well as for special plastic tests such as scratch resistance and writing effect according to Opel specifications. The device offers a significant reduction in workload for series tests, with reproducible and meaningful results.
Design and Function
The SCRATCH HARDNESS TESTER 430 P-Smart is a robust benchtop instrument with a protective cover and touch panel operation. The test procedure is fully automatic, with parameters such as cutting speed, stroke, and cross-cut pattern set via the keyboard. Each motion sequence is driven by a separate step motor, ensuring precise control over transport, cut positioning, and pressure adjustment. The specimen is conveyed linearly at a constant speed under the test tip, which can be set to a maximum pressure load of 40 N. The instrument includes two interchangeable control plates for different cross-cut patterns. Parallel cross hatch cuts with graduated test forces are possible, and up to 80 test tracks with 0.5 mm spacing can be programmed. Four versions are available, differing in manual or motor-driven force regulation and sample rotation. Motor-driven versions allow for trial runs with gradually increasing force to determine the required force for through cuts. An optional 6-piece weight set enables special tests in the lower pressure range (1–15 N, in 1-N steps).
Special Features
2 cutting speeds and 2 cutting lengths, combinable as needed
9 preset cross-cuts compliant with common standards
1 freely programmable cross-cut pattern for special applications
Step motor precision for cut distance setting
Stop option within cross hatch mode for individual test force adjustment per scratch track
Visual display when cutting through insulating layers to metal substrate
Rapid clamping device for test panels with wide clamping range
Cross Hatch Testing
The tester supports cross hatch tests according to all usual standards, with selectable cross-cuts (e.g., 2 x 5, 6 x 1, 6 x 2, 6 x 3, 8 x 1, 8 x 2, 11 x 1). Cuts are performed automatically at 40 mm/s. After a 90 manual rotation, the procedure is repeated. The required load for cutting through to the substrate is determined via trial runs. A magnifying glass (2.5x) is included for examination. Results are visually compared to standard patterns. The device is compatible with further cupping tests and alternative adhesion test methods.
Adhesion Test Apparatus, Model 525 (manual/inexpensive)
Scratch Resistance Testing
For Opel-compliant scratch resistance tests (GME 60280 / GMW14688), a 1 mm tip and a 20 x 2 mm grid are used with a 5 N load. Brightness variance (∆L) is measured using a colorimeter with D65 illuminant, d/8 geometry, and 27 mm aperture.
Writing Effect Testing
For Opel-compliant writing effect tests, an optional inset is mounted. The pattern is 80 cuts at 0.5 mm spacing with a 7 N load. Gloss difference is measured using a glossmeter with 60 geometry.
Special Tests
Additional scratch tests can be performed by varying:
Test tip: ball test tools (0.5/0.75/1/3 mm), asymmetric tools (cross cut/Clemen)
Test load: 50 N (2 N steps, standard), 15 N (1 N steps, optional)
Cutting grid: preset (2 x 5, 6 x 1, 6 x 2, 6 x 3, 8 x 1, 8 x 2, 11 x 1, 20 x 2, 80 x 0.5), freely programmable (max width 40 mm, 0.5 mm increments)
Cutting pattern: parallel or cross cuts
Cutting path: 25 mm or 40 mm (exchangeable guide plates)
Cutting speed: 16.7 mm/s (1 m/min) or 40 mm/sTo minimize testing time, the shortest possible cut length is selected.
Operation via App
The tester can be operated via smartphone or tablet app (available on Google Play Store/Apple Store), allowing for flexible settings, documentation, and data management.
Reference Class
All versions are supplied with a Calibration Certificate according to DIN 55350-18, including:
Actual and setting values of loading force
Scratching speed and cutting distance
Test equipment used with calibration status
Product identification
Date
Name of inspector
Comparisons are made for:
Loading force (5 values over the load range)
Cutting speed (both values with both cutting paths)
Cutting distance (e.g., 0.5 mm setting)
